rows.question: For about how long were the heaters of the tank that later exploded on Apollo 13 run on ground power before launch, and what did the investigating board say started the explosion?
rows.answer:
The heaters ran for about eight hours. Before launch, the oxygen tank No. 2 heaters were run on 65-volt ground power to empty the tank: [[oxygen-tank-2]] «[stated] Before launch it was emptied by running its heaters on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours»

The board traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in that tank: [[apollo-13-review-board]] «[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2»

The board's report called the switch failure a serious oversight that all parties share: [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] «[stated] Called the switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share»

The switches are the part at issue. They were built to a 1962 specification for 28 volts DC, and the heater specification was revised to 65 volts in 1965 without the switches being changed: [[oxygen-tank-2]] «[stated] The heater specification was revised in 1965 to 65 volts but the switches were not changed»

The notes don't state the board's cause in one sentence that names the switches. They give the electrically started fire and the switch failure as separate facts.

[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2
[stated] Called the switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share
[stated] The heater specification was revised in 1965 to 65 volts but the switches were not changed

rows.question: The landing site described in the Apollo 11 Mission Report's powered-descent section was named by an astronaut. What was first about the Gemini flight he commanded, and when was it?
rows.answer:
The landing site is Tranquility Base. The landing point is recorded in the Apollo 11 Mission Report (p.5-6): [[tranquility-base]] «[stated] Actual landing point was 0 degrees 41 minutes 15 seconds north, 23 degrees 26 minutes east». Tranquility Base was named by Neil Armstrong at touchdown: [[tranquility-base]] «[stated] Named by Neil Armstrong at touchdown: Houston, Tranquility Base here, the Eagle has landed».

Armstrong commanded Gemini 8. The first thing about that flight was the first docking of two spacecraft in orbit, and the year was 1966: [[neil-armstrong]] «[stated] Earlier commanded Gemini 8 in 1966, the first docking of two spacecraft in orbit».

The notes give only the year, not an exact date.

rows.question: The astronaut who caught German measles before Apollo 13 set off a crew swap. What office did the astronaut brought in by that swap later win, and what happened?
rows.answer:
The astronaut who caught German measles was Charlie Duke, the backup lunar module pilot. The crew swap he set off brought in Jack Swigert, who replaced Ken Mattingly as Apollo 13 command module pilot.

Swigert later won election to the US House of Representatives, but he died before taking office: [[jack-swigert]] «[stated] Was elected to the US House of Representatives in 1982 but died before taking office». The notes don't say how or when he died.

Sources: [[charlie-duke]] «[stated] Caught German measles from a friend's 3-year-old son about three weeks before the Apollo 13 launch»; [[rubella-crew-swap]] «[stated] The swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced at a press conference on 1970-04-10».

rows.question: The tank that crippled Apollo 13 was carried by a spacecraft. Which Apollo 11 crew member piloted that kind of spacecraft, and what did he do during the landing?
rows.answer:
The tank was Oxygen tank No. 2, the Apollo 13 tank whose thermostatic switches failed and caused the explosion. The notes link it to the command and service module, which the command-service-module note supports: [[command-service-module]] «[stated] Its service module carried the oxygen tanks that supplied power and air». The Apollo 13 explosion itself is recorded in [[oxygen-tank-2]] «[stated] Exploded on 1970-04-13, about 56 hours into the flight».

The Apollo 11 crew member who piloted that spacecraft was Michael Collins: [[michael-collins]] «[stated] Command module pilot of Apollo 11». The command-service-module note also links it to him as its pilot.

During the landing, Collins did not land. He «[stated] Stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing» ([[michael-collins]]).

The notes do not say more about what he did during the landing.

rows.question: How did the Cortright report describe the switch failure?
rows.answer:
The Cortright report (the Report of the Apollo 13 Review Board, June 1970) described the switch failure as a serious oversight in which all parties share. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] «[stated] Called the switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share»

The board's finding was that the explosion came from an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2. [[apollo-13-review-board]] «[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2»

The report also recommended removing all electrical equipment from inside the oxygen tank pressure vessel. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] «[stated] Recommended removing all electrical equipment from inside the oxygen tank pressure vessel»

The notes do not give the report's own wording on the thermostatic switches beyond these points.
